title: Highlights: Rall Syrah 2024 Swartland, South Africa
summary: Donavan Rall’s wines have impressed me since I first tasted them 15 years ago. This Syrah is just beautiful. Rall
content:
Donavan Rall’s wines have impressed me since I first tasted them 15 years ago. This Syrah is just beautiful.

Rall Syrah 2024 Swartland, South Africa
13% alcohol. Aged in concrete. This is quite beautiful. Floral aromatics with a slight stony edge to the sweet black cherry and berry fruits. There’s a hint of green sappiness, but also some charcoal and wood smoke. Beguiling. The palate is fresh and supple with sweet, alluring black cherry fruit, a hint of savoury olive tapenade, and also a bit of black pepper. There’s some subtle bloodiness, and a slight saltiness on the finish. Very Crozes-Hermitage from the flat lands in style, and deeply satisfying and delicious. The florals are probably more Côte-Rôtie: it’s very hard not to draw a northern Rhône parallel here. I bought two bottles, and my regret is not buying more. 95/100 (I bought this from The Wine Society in the UK)

title: Highlights: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Oregon winery Ponzi
summary: Website: https://ponzivineyards.com/ Impressed by these two from Oregon producer Ponzi, who back in 1970 became the third winery in the
content:
Website: https://ponzivineyards.com/

Impressed by these two from Oregon producer Ponzi, who back in 1970 became the third winery in the state. Since 2021 they have been owned by Bollinger.

Ponzi Vineyards Laurelwood District Chardonnay 2021 Chehalem Mountains, Willamette Valley, Oregon
13.1% alcohol. The Laurelwood soil series is windblown loess on top of ancient basalt bedrock. This comes from Ponzi’s  Avellana and Aurora Vineyards, as well as the Paloma Vineyard. 14% new oak. This is a distinctive Chardonnay with lots of flavour, ranging from white pepper and pear to richer peachy notes and then some savoury, spicy notes, with chamomile and herbs. It’s a rich Chardonnay, but not an obvious one: there’s a nice intensity in the mouth, with ginger, pepper, dried herbs and wood spice complexity, complementing the broad fruit. Really good. 94/100 (£38.50 Berry Bros & Rudd)

Ponzi Vineyards Laurelwood District Pinot Noir 2022 Chehalem Mountains, Willamette Valley, Oregon
13.8% alcohol. This is slightly muted on the nose, but then on the palate it has lovely elegance and focus, with sweet cherry and raspberry fruit and some subtle spicy oak. There’s nice complexity here. Juicy with good energy and nice acid line, with a tapering red fruit finish. Very stylish with promise for the future. 93/100

title: Highlights: Graham Beck Blanc de Blancs 2020 Robertson, South Africa
summary: Website: https://grahambeck.com/ Graham Beck is the leading producer of traditional method sparkling wine in South Africa, known as Cap Classiques.
content:
Website: https://grahambeck.com/

Graham Beck is the leading producer of traditional method sparkling wine in South Africa, known as Cap Classiques. And this is the new release of a regular favourite.

Graham Beck Blanc de Blancs 2020 Robertson, South Africa
100% Chardonnay. Just the cuvée press fraction used. 46% fermented in oak (small and large, all neutral) and the rest in stainless steel. 60 months on lees, bottled with residual sugar of 5 g/litre. This is fine, linear and delicate with good acidity supporting the bright citrus fruit, as well as subtle notes of baked bread and pastry. There’s a touch of grapefruit here, with zesty acidity finishing things off. So linear, precise and delicious. There’s a nice bitter twist on the finish. This is quite lovely. 93/100 (£21 mix six price at Majestic, which makes it great value for money)

title: Canada’s Okanagan and Similkameen Valleys (13) Pamplemousse Jus
summary: Website: https://www.pamplemoussejus.ca/ We need more wineries like this! Pamplemousse Jus is a small winery based on a farm in the
content:
Website: https://www.pamplemoussejus.ca/

We need more wineries like this! Pamplemousse Jus is a small winery based on a farm in the Summerland subregion of the Okanagan Valley, in British Columbia, Canada.

For a long time this farm has worked organically, and specialised in a hybrid called Leon Millon. They are also growing another hybrid, Seyval Blanc, and vinifera varieties Gewurztraminer, Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Seyval Blanc and Chardonnay.

The winery is a collaboration between Tyler Knight who looks after the farm, winemaker Jordan Kubek who has lots of experience both in the Okanagan (I first met her at Haywire, but she also makes the Lightning Rock wines, her own project), and James Langford-Smith (originally Australian, background in hospitality, he sells the wines mainly).

The approach is quite low-intervention/natural, and the wines are fun, and also really delicious.

Pomplemoose Jus Table White 2024 Okanagan, Canada
This is a blend of Chardonnay, Riesling and Gewurztraminer. Juicy, bright and fresh with lovely fruit. Stony, mineral and delicious. 92/100

Pomplemoose Coferment Leon Millet Gewurztraminer 2023 Okanagan, Canada
These two varieties were picked the same day. Juicy and bright, fresh and supple with red cherries and cranberries. Juicy, tart and linear. 94/100

Pomplemoose Marechal Foch 2024 Okanagan, Canada
Dense but fresh and juicy with some nice spicy depth to the fresh black cherry and blackberry fruit. There’s some grainy structure. Fine and very stylish with bright fruit and nice energy. 93/100

title: Restaurants: Singburi, amazing Thai food in Shoreditch, London, and a short but great wine list
summary: Popped into Singburi in Shoreditch this afternoon for a late lunch. Came away full, happy and itching to go back.
content:
Popped into Singburi in Shoreditch this afternoon for a late lunch. Came away full, happy and itching to go back.

London has quite a reputation for Thai cuisine these days. There’s the famed Anglothai (I’ve yet to go), and then Smoking Goat, which is brilliant (and has a great wine list: last time I went Claus Preisinger was on by the glass). Singburi also has a top reputation, and on today’s showing it lived up to it.

The dining room is bright, modern and simple, and there’s a long kitchen counter/bar, which is the best place to sit. You get to see every dish being created in front of you, and it’s a cooking over coals sort of place where even the burners the woks are on are coal-fired.

The menu is short and changes daily, with a limited number of options. The four we chose were all excellent, and you could do the whole thing with a group of four or five hungry people.

The drinks list is really good. Again, short, but brilliantly chosen, and fairly priced. The wine list is excellent, and sourced from the right people. The three wines we tried by the glass were sourced from Roland Wines and Les Caves de Pyrene. So organic, low intervention is the theme, but at a friendly price point. There is also the option for corkage, which s £33. That’s a decent amount: it puts off those just looking to save money, and you don’t feel bad for the restaurant if you take up the option.

What we ate:

Amazing chicken and pork belly, then an astonishingly good grilled pollock and possibly the best aubergine dish on earth.

What we drank:

Antonio Pedro Toto Barbadillo Espumoso de Albariza 2022 Spain
Fizz from Barbadillo in Sherry country. Palomino and Chardonnay. Fruity and bright and really pure.balanced and delicious. Rounded with cherry and lemon finishing chalky. This is lovely. 90/100 (Supplier Les Caves de Pyrene, £49 per bottle)

Christina Gelber Muskateller 2025 Carnuntum, Austria
From Christina Netzl, this is a lovely friendly orange wine. Skin fermented, five weeks on skins, aged in 500 litre vats. Floral and grapey with nice weight and good structure. Has some pear and table grape fruit. Grippy finish. 92/100 (supplier Roland Wines, £56 per bottle)

Domaine de la Pepière Muscadet de Sevre et Maine Sur Lie 2025 Loire, France
Stony textured and fruity with green apple and citrus fruit. So lovely. 92/100 (supplier Les Caves de Pyrene, £43 per bottle)

title: Highlights: Nyetimber Blanc de Blancs 2018 England
summary: Very impressed by this new release from leading English sparkling wine producer Nyetimber. Here’s a report from a visit last
content:
Very impressed by this new release from leading English sparkling wine producer Nyetimber. Here’s a report from a visit last year during vintage, for some context.

It’s the 2018 Blanc de Blancs, which came from the famously warm and abundant vintage in the UK, which was a real break-through point for English sparkling wine. Give this a year or two more on cork and it will be even more special, I reckon. It has that Dom Pérignon skill of being delicious to everyone, but also worthy a closer look by geeks.

Nyetimber Blanc de Blancs 2018 England
12% alcohol. The code on the back of the bottle allows you to find out all the technical details of this precise bottle. This is what I was told. Bottling date 22.05.2019; Riddling date 28.07.2025; Disgorging date 26.02.2026; Dosage – Residual Sugar (g/L) 9.4. This is deeply impressive. Lovely fruit on the nose with sweet pear and white peach as well as ripe citrus fruit, combining well with subtle toasty autolytic characters that are lurking in the background. The palate is rich, generous and fruity but has lovely lemony focus and some crystalline character, finishing long and tapering. No rough edges here, with everything integrating perfectly and an overall sense of harmony and approachability, combined with complexity. This is a beautiful wine, and it’s really serious. 95/100

title: Canada’s Okanagan and Similkameen Valleys (12) Haywire and Garnet Valley Ranch
summary: Website: https://haywirewinery.com/ I’ve reported on the wines of Okanagan star Haywire a lot in the past. Under the hands of
content:
Website: https://haywirewinery.com/

I’ve reported on the wines of Okanagan star Haywire a lot in the past. Under the hands of winemaker Matt Dumayne, with the investment and vision of owners Chris Coletta and Steve Lornie, this has become one of the go-tos for delicious Okanagan wine made in a lower-intervention style with an aversion to small oak and a love of concrete élevage.

Last year I revisited the Garnet Valley where they have planted a spectacular vineyard. I remember my first time here in July 2014 when the vines had just gone into the ground. Now, 11 years later, they looked impressive, despite the winter frost event the valley had just struggled with. I also visited in 2018.

These are the wines we tasted.

Haywire Double Bub 2016 Okanagan, Canada (magnum)
This is traditional method fizz. Toast, spice and citrus on the nose. Lively with a slight savoury twist to the stony citrus fruit. Lovely complexity here with fine toast and spice. 93/100

Haywire Freeform Blanc de Blanc 2019 Garnet Valley Ranch, Okanagan, Canada
Lovely balance: pure, fresh and linear. This has nice citrus drive with lemony focus and a nice acid line. Such precision. 93/100

Garnet Valley Ranch Chardonnay 2022 Okanagan, Canada
From 600 m elevation. Fine, fresh and pure with lovely linear citrus fruit and some real delicacy. There’s some richness here but also lovely taut fruit. Precise and even a bit saline. 94/100

Haywire Chardonnay King Family Vineyard 2022 Naramata, Okanagan, Canada
Nice detail here with lemon and white peach. This has really lovely acidity. Fruity with a hint of nut and wax in the background. Lovely stuff. 93/100

Haywire Free Form Riesling 2022 Garnet Valley Ranch, Okanagan
Full colour. This is powerful and lively with a lovely citrus drive and a crystalline quality. This has peach, toast and lime. It’s complex with lively intensity and some development. 94/100

Haywire Gamay Rosé 2022 Okanagan, Canada
Sappy with a hint of wild herbs, and nice citrus and strawberry fruit. Lovely focus. Juicy and lovely with nice cherry notes. Stylish. 91/100

Haywire Gamay 2022 West Kelowna, Okanagan, Canada
75% whole bunch. Sappy with nice grip and a stony mineral edge. Nice strawberry too with good concentration. Juicy and lively with nice complexity. 93/100

Garnet Valley Ranch Pinot Noir 2022 Okanagan, Canada
This is mostly 828 clone, and it’s 50% whole bunch. Lovely vibrant, juicy, midweight cherry and plum fruit with a touch of raspberry. Grainy and grippy with lovely fruit. So expressive with a stony, salty edge. 94/100

title: Canada’s Okanagan and Similkameen Valleys (11) Solvero in Garnet Valley
summary: Website: https://solverowines.ca/ Solvero is an exciting small winery in the Garnet Valley, which is a spectacular spot in the Summerland
content:
Website: https://solverowines.ca/

Solvero is an exciting small winery in the Garnet Valley, which is a spectacular spot in the Summerland district of the Okanagan. It’s a 30 acre site with 16 acres under vine, and it’s the project of Cass and Matt Sartor.

The name of the farm is Wildhorse Road, and at 600 metres this is one of the highest vineyards in the Okanagan, with steep terrain. After some consideration on rootstock and vine material choice, they planted 7 clones of Pinot Noir in 2016 and 2 clones of Chardonnay in 2017. Gamay has also joined the crowd. As well as their estate fruit, they also source some grapes from the Kozuki family in Happy Valley, another part of Summerland.

Matt made the first Pinot Noir in 2020, but since 2021 the wines have been made by Alison Moyes.

Solvero Pinot Gris 2023 Summerland, Okanagan, Canada
13.4% alcohol. 50% oak, 50% stainless steel. This is made from grapes supplied by the Kozuki family in Happy Valley. Very light, bright and pure with a nice appley edge to the citrus fruit. Juicy and refined. Crystalline and taut. 92/100

Solvero Chardonnay 2022 Garnet Valley, Summerland, Okanagan, Canada
13.5% alcohol. Clones 76 and 95. Barrel fermented, 16% new oak. With a subtle nuttiness this is very refined and focused, showing lovely purity. Slightly stony. This is subtle and refined, and very fine. 95/100

Solvero Pinot Noir 2020 Garnet Valley, Summerland, Okanagan, Canada
13% alcohol. Seven different clones. 30% new oak. Juicy, pure and light, but still full flavoured. Really refined with nice precision, showing real elegance and focus. Beautifully poised. 94/100

Solvero Pinot Noir 2021 Garnet Valley, Summerland, Okanagan, Canada
Sweetly textured with lovely ripe cherry and redcurrant fruit, showing good depth with dried herb notes, and peppery hints. Juicy and fine, this is expressive, and has just the faintest hint of smoke. 93/100

title: Kranz, a leading Pfalz winery, celebrates 25 years of making a single-vineyard wine from a special site called Kalmit
summary: Website: www.weingut-kranz.de Weingut Kranz is an important Pfalz winery, and recently I visited to join in with the celebrations of
content:
Website: www.weingut-kranz.de

Weingut Kranz is an important Pfalz winery, and recently I visited to join in with the celebrations of 25 years of their making wines from the Kalmit vineyard, which is located on the Kleine Kalmit in the village of Ilbesheim.

The estate dates back to 1947, but back then it was mixed agriculture, not just wine. When Boris Kranz, the current owner, joined the family estate in the mid-1990s, he recognized the potential of Kalmit, although it wasn’t until 2009 it as officially recognized as a single-vineyard site, an Einzellage. Interestingly, this was the first newly registered single-vineyard site in Germany since 1971, which was the year of the now infamous German Wine Law.

Kranz joined the VdP in 2012, so their first Grosses Gewächs (GG) wine from Kalmit was from the 2011 vintage. They had been making a single-vineyard wine from Kalmit since 2000, when they made a Riesling from here. Kalmit is unusual in that three different varieties, Riesling, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Noir, can be used to make a GG from this Grosse Lage.

Physically, Kalmit is a special site. It’s a south-facing slope with tertiary limestone soils. Specifically, this means a mix of rocks, small pieces of limestone, clay and marl-rich topsoil of differing depths.

Boris Kranz and his son Xaver presented this tasting.

Kranz Kalmit Riesling 2000 Pfalz, Germany
Dry, textural and intense with some notes of honey and wax, as well as some spiciness. Lemon and lime with nice intensity and focus, showing a slight saltiness. Powerful and layered with richness, a touch of marmalade development, and a long finely spiced finish. 95/100

Kranz Kalmit Riesling 2003 Pfalz, Germany
Beeswax, honey and a lot of spice as well as crystalline citrus fruit. Such presence and intensity with a touch of toasty development, as well as some sweet notes. Lovely depth to this wine. 94/100

Kranz Kalmit Riesling Terrassenlage 2008 Pfalz, Germany
Lovely crystalline citrus on the nose with some fine spicy detail. Intense palate with high acidity and more crystalline citrus. Lemony depth, finishing really spicy with lots of acidity. Intense style. 95/100

Kranz Kalmit Riesling Terrassenlage 2010 Pfalz, Germany
Full golden colour. Bold, rich and honeyed with a savoury spiciness and a twist of bitterness on the finish. This is showing quite a bit of development. It’s a little awkward at the moment. 91/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Riesling GG 2011 Pfalz, Germany (magnum)
Full yellow in colour. This is rich, complex and powerful with an amazing acid line threading through the lemon and lime fruit, with a hint of apricot and then some saltiness. Really vivid and distinctive. 95/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Riesling GG 2014 Pfalz, Germany
Complex nose of honey, a hint of cabbage, toast and some lime. The palate is lively with crystalline citrus fruit and nice acidity. There’s a slight bitterness on the finish. 91/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Riesling GG 2016 Pfalz, Germany
The first vintage where they were 100% organically certified. A wet start to the growing season, and then it finished dry. Nice concentration of pure lemony fruit with lovely fresh, layered, refined fruit and good acidity. Has a real sense of freshness, and finishes juicy and mouth-watering. 95/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Riesling GG 2023 Pfalz, Germany
This was wild ferment and whole cluster pressing for the first time. Juicy and lively with primary citrus fruit. This is compact and crystalline with a salt and chalk edge to the crisp fruit, finishing with wet stone minerality. Lots of potential here. 94/100

Weissburgunder was first planted here in 2003. It had been on Kalmit in the past, but had been replaced with Riesling. They made the first wine in 2006. These are all stainless steel fermented.

Kranz Kalmit Weisser Burgunder 2006 Pfalz, Germany
Honey, toast and spice with real depth of fruit. Some orange peel and lemon here, with good acidity, and a slight bitter pithy edge. Lots to like about this wine, which has developed in interesting ways. 93/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Weisser Burgunder GG 2011 Pfalz, Germany
Lively, bright and pristine with lovely pear and peach as well as keen citrus, as well as a slight toastiness. Lovely depth here with a nice acid line. Such precision and focus. Really good. 94/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Weisser Burgunder GG 2012 Pfalz, Germany
Compact with nice pear and white peach, showing good concentration as well as lovely focused acidity. Real precision here with depth but also refinement. Really nice freshness and presence. Beautiful. 95/100

Kranz Ilbesheimer Kalmit Weisser Burgunder GG 2021 Pfalz, Germany
This year they switched from stainless steel fully to small French oak. The previous year they had tried half and half. Refined nose of toast and crystalline citrus fruit. Lovely acidity here with a nice stony minerality high up in the mix. Finishes focused and linear with a slight salinity. Very refined. 94/100

Kranz Kalmit Spätburgunder 2007 Pfalz, Germany
This was the first year, and they used new oak. There’s a warmth and richness to the fruit here: the alcohol seems to be quite high and adds some sweetness to the fruit. Cherries, plums and raspberries with some warm spiciness, and a touch of oak. A very rich style that’s ageing quite well. 91/100

Kranz Ilbersheimer Kalmit Spätburgunder GG 2011 Pfalz, Germany
Small French oak here. There’s warmth, depth and richness here with sweet strawberries, some raspberry and then some dried herbs. Smooth on the finish with some earthy development. Attractive, but fully developed. 90/100

Kranz Ilbersheimer Kalmit Spätburgunder GG 2013 Pfalz, Germany
A cold vintage. A change in style, looking for more freshness and acidity, as well as lower alcohol. Fresh cherries and raspberries with some dried herbs and a touch of mint. Nicely spicy on the palate with an appealing finish. Has some spicy development. 92/100

Kranz Ilbersheimer Kalmit Spätburgunder GG 2015 Pfalz, Germany
A warm vintage, getting cool at the beginning of September. Supple and quite fresh, but also showing nice fruit ripeness. Has nice density on the palate, with red cherries and raspberries, as well as good texture. Some dried herb complexity here with a touch of orange peel. Nice fresh finish. 93/100

title: Gallery: in the Mosel, just before harvest
summary: The Mosel is a stunning wine region. I was filming here in September 2024, just before harvest, and these are
content: The Mosel is a stunning wine region. I was filming here in September 2024, just before harvest, and these are some shots. Interesting to see that Riesling can look quite different depending on vine age, genetic material and terroir, as well as with different training and pruning decisions.
